about: Bowed low, with his joined hands resting on the altar, the priest asks God that the offering be carried by the hands of His holy Angel to the altar on high before the divine majesty. The prayer does not name the Angel. The clause beginning with “ut” leads to “repleámur”: those who receive the Body and Blood of Christ ask to be filled with every blessing and grace.

seg.nr: The priest bows low and lays his joined hands upon the altar.

seg.tr: We humbly ask You, almighty God: command that Your holy Angel carry these offerings in his hands to Your altar on high, before Your divine majesty:

fn.w001: An adjective referring to those who pray: “we, the suppliants”. The translation renders it adverbially as “humbly”.
fn.w007: An accusative neuter plural: the subject of the infinitive “perférri” (w008).
fn.w008: Present passive infinitive of “pérfero”: “to be carried”.
fn.w012: Singular: one unnamed angel. The prayer does not identify him.

seg.tr: so that all of us who

fn.w023: Introduces the clause whose verb is “repleámur” (w041). An extended relative clause stands between the conjunction and its verb.
fn.w024: Nominative plural, serving as the subject of “sumpsérimus” (w035).

seg.tr: through this participation at the altar

fn.w029: Agrees with “Corpus” (w032), which follows after the rubric: “the most holy Body”.

seg.nr: The priest joins his hands and makes the sign of the cross once over the Host and once over the chalice.

seg.tr: shall receive the most holy Body and Blood of Your Son,

fn.w035: The form can be a future perfect or a perfect subjunctive. The translation follows the first analysis: “shall receive”.

seg.tr: may be filled with every heavenly blessing and grace.

fn.w040: An ablative with “repleámur” (w041): that with which one is filled.

seg.tr: Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
